name: 4-way stop: two cars arrive together
meaning: Car A (heading north) and car B (heading west) arrive at an all-way stop at the same time. B is on A's right.

name: Left turn on a green light with oncoming traffic
meaning: Car A is turning left on a circular green light while car B approaches from the opposite direction going straight.

name: School bus stopped on a two-lane road
meaning: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm out on a two-lane road; car A approaches from the opposite direction.

name: Emergency vehicle approaching from behind
meaning: An ambulance with flashing lights is coming up behind car A on a two-lane road; A pulls to the right edge and stops.

name: All-way stop: first to arrive goes first
meaning: At an all-way stop, car A (heading north) is already stopped at its stop line while car B (heading west, on A's right) is still approaching its stop sign.

name: All-way stop: left turn vs. straight
meaning: At an all-way stop, car A (heading north, signaling left) and oncoming car B (heading south, going straight) have stopped at the same time.

name: Uncontrolled intersection
meaning: Car A (heading east) and car B (heading north, on A's right) reach an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time.

name: T-intersection with no signs
meaning: Car A on a side road that ends at a through road is about to turn left, while car B approaches on the through road from A's right; there are no signs or signals.

name: Left turn on a flashing yellow arrow
meaning: Car A is turning left on a flashing yellow left arrow (shown in the close-up) while oncoming car B goes straight.

name: Right turn on red with a pedestrian
meaning: Car A is stopped at a red light, signaling a right turn, while a pedestrian walks across the crosswalk directly in front of it.

name: Right turn while a pedestrian crosses
meaning: Car A has a green light and is turning right while a pedestrian crosses the street A is turning into.

name: Green light, but no room past the intersection
meaning: Car A has a green light, but traffic is backed up right to the far side of the intersection; the shaded area is where A would be stuck, blocking car B, which is waiting on the cross street.

name: Traffic signal out of power
meaning: The traffic lights at an intersection are completely dark (power out); car A (heading north) and car B (heading west, on A's right) have both stopped.

name: Driving through a roundabout
meaning: Car A entered a roundabout from the south, travels counterclockwise around the center island, and signals right as it nears its exit to the west.

name: Two-way left-turn lane
meaning: Car A is stopped in a shared center left-turn lane, signaling a left turn into a driveway, while oncoming car B approaches in its own lane.

name: Left turn onto a multi-lane road
meaning: Car A is in the left lane of a road with two lanes each way and is turning left onto another two-lane-each-way road; its destination lanes are marked 1 (next to the center line) and 2.

name: Truck making a wide right turn
meaning: A large truck is signaling a right turn from the left lane so it can swing wide; car A is coming up in the right lane into the space beside the truck (shaded).

name: Emergency vehicle while you are in an intersection
meaning: Car A is in the middle of an intersection when a fire truck with flashing lights comes up behind it; A's path continues through and pulls to the right after the intersection.

name: Leaving a driveway
meaning: Car A is leaving a driveway, signaling right, and has stopped before the sidewalk, where a pedestrian is walking; car B is approaching on the street in the lane A wants to enter.

name: Pedestrian with a white cane
meaning: A pedestrian carrying a white cane is crossing at a crosswalk in front of car A, which has stopped at the stop line.

name: Yielding when entering a roundabout
meaning: Car A is stopped at the yield line of a roundabout entry while car B, already circulating counterclockwise, is about to pass in front of A's entry from A's left.

name: Yield sign where a side road joins
meaning: Car A is on an angled side road with a yield sign where it joins a through road; car B is approaching on the through road in the lane A wants to enter.

name: Behind a stopped school bus
meaning: Car A is behind a school bus that is stopped in the same lane with red lights flashing and its stop arm out while children cross the road in front of it.

name: Police car stopped on the shoulder
meaning: A police car with flashing lights is stopped on the right shoulder of a two-lane one-way roadway behind a pulled-over car; car A, in the right lane, moves over to the left lane.

name: Large truck No-Zones
meaning: Shaded areas mark a large truck's No-Zones (front, rear and both sides); car A is beside the truck in its right-side No-Zone and car B is in the left lane well behind the truck.

name: Passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road
meaning: On a two-lane road, car A is behind bicyclist C riding near the right edge while car B approaches in the oncoming lane.

name: Right turn across a bike lane
meaning: Car A is signaling to turn right at an intersection while bicyclist B rides straight ahead in the bike lane on A's right.

name: Car door opening into a bike lane
meaning: Parked car A has its driver door open into the bike lane while bicyclist B rides toward the door.

name: Railroad crossing with gates down
meaning: At a railroad crossing the red lights are flashing and the gates are down while a train approaches; car A is stopped before the stop line.

name: Merging onto a freeway
meaning: Car A is in the acceleration lane of a freeway on-ramp, signaling left to merge into the gap between car C and car B in the right lane.

name: Car in the blind spot
meaning: Car A is signaling to move into the left lane while car B is beside and slightly behind it in A's blind spot (shaded).

name: Solid yellow line on your side
meaning: Car A is following slower car B on a two-lane road; the center line is solid yellow on A's side and broken yellow on the other side.

name: Broken yellow line on your side
meaning: Car A is following slower car B on a two-lane road; the center line is broken yellow on A's side and solid on the other side, and an arrow shows A passing B.

name: Counting following distance
meaning: Car B has just passed a roadside tree; car A, behind B, counts the seconds until it reaches the same tree.

name: Parked uphill with a curb
meaning: Car A is parked facing uphill next to a curb with its front wheels turned away from the curb (to the left).

name: Parked downhill with a curb
meaning: Car A is parked facing downhill next to a curb with its front wheels turned toward the curb (to the right).

name: Parked uphill with no curb
meaning: Car A is parked facing uphill at the edge of a road with no curb, its front wheels turned toward the edge of the road (to the right).

name: Work-zone flagger showing STOP
meaning: In a work zone, a flagger at the right side of the road holds a STOP paddle toward car A, which is stopping.

name: Farm tractor ahead
meaning: Car A is behind farm tractor B, which shows an orange-and-red slow-moving-vehicle triangle, on a two-lane road.

name: Deer at the roadside at dusk
meaning: At dusk, car A drives with headlights on toward a deer standing at the right edge of the road with another deer behind it in the field.
